title: 5b PRD: component discovery + vocabulary
description:
## Problem Statement

Sutra discovers structural facts (Layer 0) and detects conventions (Layer 2), but has no notion of **components** — coherent groups of related code that form the architectural building blocks of a codebase. Without components, sutra cannot answer "what are the pieces of this system?", cannot scope conventions or constraints to a subsystem, cannot identify load-bearing code within a subsystem, and cannot map human concepts ("the parser", "auth flow") to code locations.

Agents starting a new session have no persistent vocabulary for navigating the codebase at an architectural level. They rediscover the same subsystem boundaries each time.

## Solution

Build the component discovery engine (Layer 1) and vocabulary layer (Layer 5) as new modules in sutra. Components are discovered via Louvain graph clustering on the file-level call/dependency graph, reconciled against persistent durable entities that carry human intent (names, lifecycle state, aliases). The vocabulary layer provides a human-to-code mapping so agents and humans can refer to code by concept ("the parser") rather than path.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want sutra to automatically discover the major subsystems in my codebase from its call graph, so that I have an architectural map without manual annotation.
2. As a developer, I want components to persist across recomputation with stable names and IDs, so that my annotations (names, aliases, lifecycle) survive when the code evolves.
3. As a developer, I want to see when components merge, split, or drift between clustering runs, so that I'm alerted to architectural changes I didn't intend.
4. As a developer, I want to mark a component as "sketching" so that conventions become informational rather than enforced while I'm prototyping.
5. As a developer, I want sutra to identify semantic anchors (load-bearing types/functions) per component, so that agents and humans know where to start reading.
6. As a developer, I want a concept density metric per component, so that I can prioritize review attention on dense (hard to understand per LOC) areas.
7. As an agent, I want to resolve human concepts ("the parser", "auth flow") to specific files and components, so that I can navigate the codebase using the vocabulary humans use.
8. As a developer, I want to define aliases in `.sutra/aliases.toml` that map my terminology to code locations, so that the vocabulary reflects how I think about my codebase.
9. As a developer, I want sutra to detect when my aliases point at dissolved components or deleted paths, so that I can fix stale vocabulary.
10. As a developer, I want component discovery to respect language-specific module boundaries (Rust's `mod` system as strong signal, weaker for Python/C), so that clustering aligns with language idioms.
11. As a developer, I want clustering to recompute lazily only when the structural graph has changed meaningfully, so that it's not wasted on lint fixes or comment edits.
12. As a developer, I want to override the clustering resolution parameter in `.sutra/components.toml`, so that I can control granularity when auto-tuning doesn't match my architecture.
13. As an agent, I want `sutra orient` to include which component I'm working in plus its semantic anchors, so that I have architectural context before writing code.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Algorithm:** Louvain community detection on file-level call/dependency graph with 1/ambiguity edge weighting. Single-level sufficient at tested scales. Resolution parameter auto-tuned (target reasonable component count per codebase size) with human override via `.sutra/components.toml`.
- **Recomputation trigger:** Lazy — on first query after staleness detected. Stale when (a) files added/removed, or (b) >10% of inter-file edges changed since last clustering run. Edge count at last clustering stored in a metadata row.
- **Component identity:** Components are durable entities (UUID, name, lifecycle_state, created_at, updated_at). Membership is ephemeral (recomputed). Reconciliation on recompute via Jaccard overlap: >0.6 → match existing component; no match → create new; existing component unmatched → mark dissolved (kept in DB, hidden from normal queries).
- **Events:** Merge (two components collapsed), split (one became two), drift (>30% file shift). Stored durably in `component_events` table, surfaced in review reports.
- **Lifecycle:** Per-component, not per-file. Enum: `sketching | stable`. Sketching flattens conventions to informational; constraints remain enforced.
- **Semantic anchors:** Identified by in-degree within component, betweenness centrality, git stability, naming alignment. 3-7 per component. Stored ephemeral, recomputed alongside membership.
- **Concept density:** v1 metric from Layer 0 data: `(unique_symbol_kinds × naming_stem_diversity) / LOC`. Richer FCA-based version deferred to 5c.
- **Vocabulary resolution priority:** (1) human aliases from `.sutra/aliases.toml`, (2) component names, (3) semantic anchor names. HRR fuzzy matching deferred to post-v1.
- **Auto-learning:** Not in v1. Explicit aliases only.
- **Auto-naming:** Longest common path prefix of member files, stripped to last segment. Fallback: most-central file's parent directory.
- **Dissolved components:** Kept in DB marked dissolved with timestamp. Aliases pointing at them become orphaned, surfaced in reconciliation report.
- **Adapter extension:** `module_boundary_hints()` added to `LanguageAdapter` trait with default `Weak`. Rust → `Strong`, Dart → `Moderate`. Clustering uses this to weight language module boundaries in the graph.
- **Storage partition:** `components` (durable), `component_membership` (ephemeral), `semantic_anchors` (ephemeral), `component_events` (durable), `aliases` (durable). Follows 5a ephemeral/durable pattern — durable tables reference by name/path, not integer PK.
- **New modules:** `src/components/mod.rs` (discovery engine), `src/components/anchors.rs` (anchor identification), `src/components/config.rs` (configuration), `src/vocabulary/mod.rs` (alias CRUD + resolution), `src/db/components.rs` (schema + queries).
- **Dependency:** Builds on `graph.rs::build_file_adjacency` for the call graph input. Adds `louvain` algorithm (likely vendored or thin crate — community_detection or petgraph-based).

## Testing Decisions

Tests should verify external behavior through the module's public interface, not implementation details.

**Modules under test:**

1. **Discovery engine (`src/components/mod.rs`)** — integration tests with synthetic call graphs:
   - Known file adjacency → produces expected cluster count and composition
   - Reconciliation: given prior components + new clustering → correct match/create/dissolve decisions
   - Merge detection: two prior components whose files now cluster together → merge event emitted
   - Split detection: one prior component whose files now span two clusters → split event emitted
   - Drift detection: >30% file shift → drift event emitted
   - Staleness: edge changes below threshold → no recompute; above threshold → recompute

2. **Vocabulary resolver (`src/vocabulary/mod.rs`)** — unit tests:
   - Alias defined in DB → resolves correctly
   - Component name match → resolves when no alias exists
   - Anchor name match → resolves as fallback
   - Priority: alias wins over component name wins over anchor
   - Orphan detection: alias pointing at dissolved component → flagged
   - `.sutra/aliases.toml` parsing: valid TOML → correct alias entries

**Prior art:** Existing tests in `tests/` (integration style, use `Db::open_unchecked` with temp dirs). Follow the same pattern.

## Out of Scope

- HRR embed-mode fuzzy matching for vocabulary (deferred — no HRR infrastructure yet)
- Auto-learning from agent sessions (deferred to post-v1 with curation UX)
- Convention scoping to components (that's 5c's concern, but will consume component membership)
- Constraint scoping to components (that's 5d's concern)
- Component visualization / UI (separate concern per architecture doc)
- Multi-level Louvain / hierarchical components (not needed at tested scales)
- Health metrics per component (that's 5e's concern, but will consume component membership)

## Further Notes

- The Louvain implementation should be pure Rust with no external process. The `louvain_communities` crate or a custom implementation on petgraph are both viable — evaluate at implementation time.
- The reconciliation algorithm is the most subtle part. Edge cases: a codebase's first clustering (no prior components — all creates), a major refactor that shuffles everything (many dissolves + creates vs. few drifts), and the degenerate case where the whole codebase is one cluster.
- Component events feed directly into the review report (5b produces the data; the review tool in `tools/review.rs` will consume it). The event schema should be designed for easy rendering.
- The `.sutra/components.toml` file is optional — sutra works with pure auto-tuning by default (zero-config principle from the vision doc).
